text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David.
When the Ziphites came and told Saul, "Isn't David hiding among us?"
Save me, O God, by your name; vindicate me by your might.
Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life; they have not set God before them. Selah

versions.text: For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life; they give no thought to God. Selah
versions.explanation: The idiom "they have not set God before them" is more concrete than the abstract paraphrase and preserves the image of God being placed in view; it also matches the perfect-tense verbs of the preceding clauses.

text: But see, God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my life.

versions.text: But see, God is my helper; the Lord is the one who sustains me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has נַפְשִׁי ("my life/soul"), which is lost in "sustains me." Restoring it keeps the parallel with verse 5 ("ruthless men seek my life") and reads well aloud.

text: He will turn the evil back on my foes; in your faithfulness, put an end to them.

versions.text: He will turn their evil back on those who slander me; in your faithfulness, put an end to them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "he will return the evil to my watchers/foes." The current wording mismatches persons ("their evil ... on those who slander me") and the possessive "their" has no antecedent. Also, שֹׁרְרָי means adversaries who lie in wait/watch me, not specifically slanderers.

text: I will sacrifice to you with a freewill offering; I will praise your name, O LORD, for it is good.
For he has delivered me from every trouble, and my eye has looked in triumph on my enemies.
